life_history_notes: Pacific Northwest Bumble Bee Atlas surveys found the species most often in developed areas and meadows, with records in other habitat categories. Frequently recorded floral resources included phacelias, lupines and raspberries; this evidence describes the Pacific Northwest atlas area.
Introduced to North America; social colonies store honey and pollen. Managed and feral colonies make this species relevant when assessing floral-resource use by native bees.
